title: Tenant telemetry isolation and per-tenant fast-fail policy to contain 5xx surges
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a multi-tenant traffic surge on 2026-02-28 we observed correlated 5xx bursts that propagated through the streaming and batch RPC paths. Root cause analysis shows a combination of downstream transient errors, broad optimistic retry behavior in the edge proxy, and insufficient per-tenant telemetry isolation which made it difficult to identify and quarantine noisy tenants quickly. This ticket implements a rollback-safe containment strategy: (1) per-tenant telemetry signatures to rapidly fingerprint and surface noisy traffic, (2) a lightweight per-tenant fast-fail policy at the edge to cut retries for tenants exhibiting repeated downstream 5xx patterns, and (3) a guided client-side retry advisory surfaced via SDK headers and Console incident UI.
implementation_notes: Edge proxy changes: add per-tenant counters for 5xx/timeout rate (rolling window 60s) and a decision FSM that transitions tenant->FASTFAIL after threshold (configurable). FASTFAIL mode returns a 429/451 with guidance headers and suppresses backend fanout; it also stops optimistic retries for that tenant for a cooldown period. Streaming path: ensure streaming sessions include tenant-id in trace headers and add backpressure signal so an identified FASTFAIL tenant can be signaled without tearing existing streams. Telemetry: emit a tenant.signature hash + sample of request fingerprints to a dedicated metrics namespace to speed query. SDK/Console: SDK will honor new guidance header X-Redwood-Retry-Advisory and automatically back off (opt-in safe mode). Console will surface an incident card with affected tenants and one-click opt-out to route to dedicated capacity. All changes are feature-flagged and controlled by runtime config with default OFF for 48-hour canary and gradual rollout to 10%/50%/100% across regions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for FSM transitions, integration tests validating header propagation and retry suppression, chaos test that injects synthetic downstream 502s for a tenant and validates that only the noisy tenant toggles FASTFAIL while others remain unaffected. Load test to ensure per-tenant counters scale (controlled against dev cluster). Observability validation: dashboards show clear signal, and we add alerting rule: if >3 tenants enter FASTFAIL within 5m, page SRE. Canary run in us-west-2 for 48h with synthetic tenants, then staged rollout.
rollout_and_rollback: Rollout steps: merge behind feature flag -> deploy edge-proxy canary (10% traffic) + monitoring -> enable telemetry read-only -> enable FASTFAIL for synthetic tenants -> increase traffic fraction to 50% after 24h -> full rollout. Rollback: flip feature flag OFF to immediately stop FASTFAIL decisioning (edge will stop returning advisory codes), revert proxy binary if necessary. All rollout stages include automated health gates (5xx rate, latency P95, downstream error amplification).
customer_communication: Notify customers impacted in the incident postmortem and offer temporary routing to Dedicated or Private if they require hard isolation. For customers who saw elevated retries/timeouts, we will provide a short technical note explaining the FASTFAIL advisory header and how to opt-in/out in SDKs. Support playbook updated to recommend enabling SDK safe-mode and using dedicated capacity for bursty ingestion workloads.
postmortem_and_followups: Follow-ups: (1) permanent telemetry index for tenant-signatures to support fast queries in Console (ENG-580211), (2) expand SDK safe-mode to include configurable exponential backoff with jitter, (3) evaluate automatic tenant throttles with customer opt-in and billing guardrails, (4) add a regression test suite to CI to catch retry amplification scenarios. Assign owners for each follow-up and schedule a 2-week reliability retrospective with SRE and Product.
